contributions.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' line 1 TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED (3.46) on the p2 Summary Page, which is also Schedule A's own printed 'Subtotal for this page $ 3.46' AND its printed 'Total Contributions Received $ 3.46', and is repeated at summary line 4 'Total Contributions Received (From Line 1 Column A)' = 3.46
contributions.detail: The single Schedule A row sums to 3.46 = the schedule's printed page subtotal (3.46) = the schedule's printed Total Contributions Received (3.46) = the cover's promoted PER-PERIOD cell Column A (3.46). Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' prints 503.46 and is NOT summed as an increment (utah is a per-period regime). THE LOAN QUESTION WAS DECIDED BY THE ARITHMETIC, the opposite way from Witney 2010 (ADDENDUM A4): the row's donor cell reads 'Personal Loan', but here the cover assigns it to line 1 CONTRIBUTIONS, not to line 3 Balance at Beginning — line 3 prints a NEGATIVE (3.46) in hand-drawn accounting parentheses, and the ladder closes only that way: line 5 Subtotal = line 3 + line 4 = -3.46 + 3.46 = 0 (printed as a slashed zero), line 7 Balance at Close = line 5 - line 6 = 0 - 0 = 0 (printed as a slashed zero). So the personal loan IS this filing's itemized contribution row.

expenditures.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' line 2 TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE, written as a SLASHED ZERO (read 0 under the repo zero-glyph ruling), matched by Schedule B's own printed 'Subtotal for this page $ -0-' and its printed 'Total Expenditures Received $ Ø'
expenditures.detail: Schedule B (p4) is present and every one of its 16 ruled rows is BLANK - no date, no payee, no address, no amount anywhere on the grid. The filer wrote the nil mark '-0-' on the page subtotal line and a slashed zero on the Total Expenditures Received line; both denote the digit zero under the repo zero-glyph ruling and both agree with the cover's promoted per-period cell (Column A line 2, also a slashed zero) and with summary line 6 'Total Expenditures Made (From Line 2 Column A)', also a slashed zero. Zero rows is the honest reading: the schedule EXISTS and the filer entered nothing. Column B YTD 503.46 is cumulative and never summed.

itemized.notes: Page-face candidate 'Robert Kirk', Republican, 'Utah County Treasurer' - index.csv names NO candidate for this row (its `candidate` cell is empty; the channel label is the period string 'Kirk - 10/26/10'), so the page face supplies the name. 4 pages, each classified from its own printed header: p1 COVER (2010 FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN REPORT FOR COUNTY CANDIDATES, Utah County Code 2-5 & Utah State Code 17-16-6.5; report type 'Seven days preceding the General Election' ticked; 'Is this report an amendment? No' ticked; signed and dated 10/26/2010; clerk date stamp OCT 26 PM 3:47), p2 SUMMARY PAGE (found at the usual legacy_colAB position but located by its printed 'SUMMARY PAGE' heading, not by ordinal), p3 SCHEDULE A - ITEMIZED CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED, p4 SCHEDULE B - ITEMIZED EXPENDITURES MADE. The filer foliates his own sheets 2/3/4 'of 4' in the top-right block, so foliation INCLUDES the cover here - the opposite of Poulson's 2010 practice (ADDENDUM A4) and one more reason an ordinal never locates a page. SUMMARY LADDER, verbatim: line 1 = 3.46 / 503.46; line 2 = slashed zero / 503.46; line 3 = (3.46) written inside hand-drawn parentheses, i.e. a NEGATIVE beginning balance of -3.46; line 4 = 3.46; line 5 = slashed zero; line 6 = slashed zero; line 7 = slashed zero. The ladder is internally exact. A NEGATIVE BALANCE AT BEGINNING IS REAL here, as it was for Poulson (ADDENDUM A4) - the campaign was 3.46 overdrawn and the personal loan of exactly 3.46 zeroes it out; that is why the itemized contribution and the beginning balance carry the same figure without either being a restatement of the other. Cycle context: Column B shows 503.46 raised and 503.46 spent year-to-date, so this final-period report itemizes only the closing 3.46; the earlier periods' donors are in the filer's earlier 2010 reports, not here. Schedule B is an EMPTY SCHEDULE, not a missing page and not an unread one.
